agents' IDs, so its launch found the earlier run's completed record (not
yet condensed) and added none, and its stop was then skipped as a
duplicate, losing the run's files, transcript and tokens. The stop now
completes a record of its own unless one already holds the same run's
transcript, whichever order the runs' stops arrive in.

feat(codex): track subagents via Codex's SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks

Codex was the one agent named in the original subagent-tracking request with zero
subagent tracking, even though it ships first-class hooks for it. Wire them.

Codex's identity fields are the opposite of what the names suggest, and getting
this backwards would attribute subagent work to a session Entire has never seen:

  - session_id is "the identity shared by the root thread and all descendant
    threads" (session/session.rs) — the *user's* session. It maps straight to
    SessionID.
  - agent_id is the subagent thread's own id. Codex sends no tool_use_id, so
    agent_id doubles as ToolUseID: it is the only value correlating a start with
    its stop, and Entire keys pre-task state (pre-task-<id>.json) and the task
    metadata directory on ToolUseID.

SubagentStop also carries two transcripts — transcript_path is the parent rollout,
agent_transcript_path the subagent's own. Rather than teach the framework a second
layout to guess, add Event.SubagentTranscriptPath so an agent can *declare* where
its subagent transcript is; handleLifecycleSubagentEnd prefers it and falls back to
the Claude Code layout guess. A declared-but-missing path warns rather than
silently substituting, because that disagreement is exactly what went unnoticed
while the guess quietly returned "" for every non-Claude agent.

That mechanism immediately fixes a second agent: Cursor has parsed

# Plan: Add Context Plumbing Throughout the CLI

## Context

`main.go` creates a cancellable context (`context.WithCancel`) and passes it to Cobra via `rootCmd.ExecuteContext(ctx)`. However, no command retrieves it via `cmd.Context()`. Instead, ~120+ production code locations create `context.Background()`, losing cancellation support from SIGINT/SIGTERM and any parent context values.

## Goal

Thread the root context from `main.go` through the entire call chain, replacing `context.Background()` with the properly propagated context. This enables signal-based cancellation to propagate to git operations, checkpoint writes, and other long-running work.
